snippet.title: The First Moonwalk - Bill Bailey - The Apollo Theatre - New York -  1955
snippet.description:
This is one of the first ever moonwalks on film
 Bill Bailey tapping to a rather quiet instrumental version of the Larks' hit "The World is Waiting for Sunrise" performed by the Paul Williams Quartet.

He's the brother of singer Pearl Bailey, but he has nothing to do with her signature song "Won't You Come Home Bill Bailey" which is a very old standard dating back to 1902.

Bill's frequently credited with "inventing" the "moonwalk" because of a tapdancing move called "backslide" which he does in this filmed performance.

snippet.title: Did Michael Jackson Steal Moonwalk from Charlie Chaplin?
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson idolized Charlie Chaplin but did he steal his infamous moonwalk and many other dance moves from Chaplin? Both Jackson the King of Pop and Chaplin the King of Silent Movies are iconic entertainers who captivated the world with their dance and overall genius. 
Flashback and watch this short side-by-side dance battle between Michael Jackson Billie Jean at the 1995 MTV Awards including Michael Jackson moonwalk vs the dancing and moonwalk of Charlie Chaplin Modern Times from 1939. 

We created this Short comparison by thoroughly researching both performances, studying the dance movements, identifying similar moments, and carefully editing selected parts of each performance side by side so viewers could compare them directly. We built the video around the question of how Charlie Chaplin may have influenced Michael Jackson’s dancing, creating a new visual comparison from two separate performances for both historical interest and entertainment. 

From the moonwalk to other similar movements, this dance-off lets you compare the performers for yourself. Without a doubt we know Chaplin was one of many Michael Jackson influences for his King of Pop Moonwalk, along with James Brown, Bill Bailey, Fred Astaire and others. 

This Short is a condensed version of our original longer Michael Jackson and Charlie Chaplin dance comparison, featuring selected moments from the same side-by-side edit.

Let's get real - when artists borrow from each other, is it a nod of respect, or do you think it's more like stealing? Let us know in the comments. Thanks for watching! 💞

snippet.title: Did Michael Jackson Steal Moonwalk from Charlie Chaplin? Extended Version
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson idolized Charlie Chaplin but did he steal his infamous moonwalk and many other dance moves from Chaplin? Both Jackson the King of Pop and Chaplin the King of Silent Movies are iconic entertainers who captivated the world with their dance and overall genius. 
Flashback and watch this extended version side-by-side dance battle between Michael Jackson Billie Jean at the 1995 MTV Awards including Michael Jackson moonwalk vs the dancing and moonwalk of Charlie Chaplin Modern Times from 1939. 

We created this comparison by researching both performances, studying the dance movements, identifying similar moments, and carefully editing selected parts of each performance side by side so viewers could compare them directly. We built the video around the question of how Charlie Chaplin may have influenced Michael Jackson’s dancing, creating a new visual comparison from two separate performances for both historical interest and entertainment. 

From the moonwalk to other similar movements, this dance-off lets you compare the performers for yourself. Without a doubt we know Chaplin was one of many Michael Jackson influences for his King of Pop Moonwalk, along with James Brown, Bill Bailey, Fred Astaire and others. 

Let's get real - when artists borrow from each other, is it a nod of respect, or do you think it's more like stealing? Let us know in the comments. Thanks for watching! 💞

snippet.title: How to Moonwalk
snippet.description:
When Michael Jackson debuted his famous "moonwalk" in 1983, the world was amazed. Once called the "backslide", knowing how to do this dance move is guaranteed to get you to shine on the dance floor.

0:00 Preparing to moonwalk
0:11 Foot placement
0:20 Basic movements
0:51 Putting it all together

-- How to Moonwalk --
1. Start by putting on a pair of socks so you have as little friction as possible while you're learning. 
2. Then, standing on a smooth surface, place one foot directly in front of the other. You want the width between your legs to be about 4 inches, which will help you keep your balance. 
3. Next, lift your back heel up so you're standing on your toes. When you're ready, slide your front foot straight back so it passes behind your other foot. 
4. Now, lift your back heel up while simultaneously lowering your front heel down. 
5. Once you've done that, slide your front foot straight back so it passes behind your other foot. 
6. From there, lift your back heel while dropping your front heel at the same time. 
7. Put it all together by smoothly alternating which foot you use to slide backwards, and you're moonwalking!

Learn to add more to your moonwalk by reading the full article here: https://www.wikihow.com/Moonwalk
